transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-12-01 15:30 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Aidan Lee (Quasar CTO), Maya Patel (Quasar ML), Sam Rogers (Quasar Infra)

Auto-summary: Quick discovery focused on embeddings/rerank flow, vector DB integration, and security. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable throughput but wants clarity on hosted performance and private deployment for data residency.

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time, um today we're gonna run through how Redwood handles embeddings and reranking workflows, and answer questions about integration with your vector DB, throughput, and security.
[00:14] Aidan Lee: Yep thanks Jordan, quick context - Quasar runs a research search product, we have an existing Milvus instance with FAISS on top for offline indexes, and we're evaluating moving embeddings + rerank to a managed inference path.
[00:29] Priya Desai: Great, so just to confirm - you're looking at two pieces right? 1) generating embeddings at scale and storing them in your vector DB, and 2) a reranker/cross-encoder that runs on top of the top-k, is that correct?
[00:39] Maya Patel: Yeah that's the idea. Our pipeline: daily embed bulk of new docs, real-time queries use hybrid search (BM25 + vector) then we run a cross-encoder rerank on top for final scoring.
[00:50] Sam Rogers: Our infra constraint is we need 500 qps at 100ms p95 for the query path; embedding generation can be batched, but latency for query path is sensitive.
[01:03] Jordan Kim: Okay good note - 500 QPS with 100ms p95 is fairly high for a hosted service unless we pick the right model and batching, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, Private gives you VPC/on-prem for full control.
[01:18] Aidan Lee: How does Redwood integrate with Milvus/FAISS? Do you host the vectors or do we?
[01:25] Priya Desai: Redwood doesn't require a specific vector DB. For Hosted customers, many push embeddings into Pinecone or our managed index, but we also support pushing embeddings back to your DB - we provide simple connectors and sample scripts for Milvus, Weaviate, and S3-backed FAISS indexes. For Dedicated/Private you typically keep vectors in your infra and call Redwood for embedding generation and reranking, or you can use Redwood-managed indexes depending on security requirements.
[01:48] Maya Patel: That connector for Milvus - is it real-time or batch? We do both.
[01:53] Priya Desai: We have both; embedding generation supports streaming and batch modes. For bulk ingestion we recommend batching with 2-4k examples per job to maximize GPU utilization. For real-time it's small minibatches or single-item streams; Redwood's runtime optimizes for KV cache reuse and continuous batching.
[02:11] Sam Rogers: You mentioned KV cache, I think in our notes it said K V cash, so sorry if it's mis-said. What's the hit on memory when we use KV caching at top-k?
[02:20] Priya Desai: Yeah - KV cache here is key/value attention cache for decoding, mostly affects autoregressive gen. For embedding + cross-encoder rerank, memory is driven by model size (dimensionality) and batch. If you're running a cross-encoder on 768 or 1,024 dims, it's lighter than a 3B gen model.
[02:37] Aidan Lee: Speaking of dims - what embedding sizes do you see customers use? We're exploring 512 vs 1536.
[02:43] Jordan Kim: 1536 is common with some open models; it's higher capacity but increases storage and index search cost. 512 or 768 embeddings are cheaper in storage/search throughput. Typical trade: higher dims give slightly better quality, but using approximate search and re-ranking you can often get away with 512 and then rerank top-100 with a stronger model.
[03:03] Maya Patel: So we'd do lower dim for the index and a heavier cross-encoder?
[03:07] Priya Desai: Exactly - hybrid approach: use efficient vector index at 512-768 dims for recall, then cross-encoder rerank (on CPU or GPU) on the top-K. That saves cost and keeps latency.
[03:17] Sam Rogers: For 500 qps, how do you size Dedicated? We need predictable p95.
[03:22] Jordan Kim: We'll size GPUs for inference throughput based on your model choice and batch patterns. For example, a quantized 1.3B embedder at 512 dims can do X qps per GPU (we'll put numbers in the sizing doc). Dedicated gives reserved capacity so you don't see noisy neighbor effects.
[03:36] Aidan Lee: Any options for hybrid search (BM25 + vector) in Redwood? We use BM25 to warm recall.
[03:42] Priya Desai: Yes - our routing supports hybrid pipelines. Two common patterns: 1) BM25 to generate candidates, then vector similarity on those, 2) vector-based retrieval + feature fusion where we combine BM25 and cosine scores with learned weights and then rerank. We also support stitching results server-side if you want to keep your BM25 in-house.
[03:59] Maya Patel: What about rerank latency? We can't add more than ~30ms on top of the retrieval for UX reasons.
[04:05] Priya Desai: Reranker latency depends on model size - small cross-encoders on CPU can be ~10-25ms for single pairs if optimized; GPUs help for batch rerank. Another architecture is to rerank only top-10 or top-20 which keeps extra latency low.
[04:18] Sam Rogers: Security question - we need SOC2 and SSO. Also, can KMS keys be customer-managed?
[04:24] Jordan Kim: Yes - Redwood is SOC 2 compliant (we'll share the cert). For Private deployment you can integrate with customer KMS/HSM and we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. Dedicated can also offer VPC peering and private link. We'll attach the security pack and architecture notes.
[04:39] Aidan Lee: If we go Hosted, are vectors retained by Redwood? Is there a delete policy?
[04:44] Priya Desai: For Hosted, we have configurable retention - and we can set auto-delete or provide encrypted-at-rest storage with customer KMS for enterprise accounts. But many enterprises prefer Private or Dedicated to keep vectors in their own VPC for compliance.
[04:58] Jordan Kim: Quick objection I hear sometimes: "Why not just run everything on our infra with FAISS?" The answer is control vs ops cost - Redwood's value is predictable inference throughput, autoscaling, and operational tooling for rollouts, traceability, and cost breakdowns. If you want full control and air-gap, Private can run in your environment.
[05:17] Maya Patel: Cost question - for reranking on top-k, is that charged per token or per inference?
[05:23] Jordan Kim: For Hosted it's per-token + per-inference for generation; embeddings and rerankers are metered per-second or per-request depending on the contract. For Dedicated we provide committed capacity pricing which smooths unit cost. We'll include both models in the pricing doc.
[05:38] Sam Rogers: Can we run an A/B between a quantized embedder and a higher-precision one? We want to test quality vs cost tradeoffs.
[05:45] Priya Desai: Absolutely - Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and measurement harness to run A/Bs on your prompt set. For embeddings you can test 512 vs 1536 dims with a rerank baseline to measure downstream impact.
[05:58] Aidan Lee: How long does a pilot usually take? We want to get results quickly - under two weeks ideally.
[06:04] Jordan Kim: Typical pilot with a sample dataset and target queries takes 5-10 business days to instrument, run benchmarks, and produce a report. Priya's benchmark template should help speed this.
[06:14] Maya Patel: Ok, for the benchmark we'll want scripts that push embeddings into our Milvus cluster and then run queries with the hybrid pipeline.
[06:21] Priya Desai: We'll share a repo with connectors and a test harness that can either write to Milvus or Redwood-managed index; it includes approximate search tuning and candidate k selection.
[06:31] Sam Rogers: Any gotchas for dimensionality when using Milvus + FAISS quantization? We saw weird recall drops with 512->int8 conversions.
[06:40] Priya Desai: Quantization can affect recall; recommended approach is PQ/HNSW combos and to validate on your eval set. Also, don't quantize embeddings for the reranker input; only quantize for index storage if necessary.
[06:54] Jordan Kim: Quick recap before we wrap - next steps: Jordan will email pricing + sizing doc, Priya will share benchmark repo and scripts, Quasar (Aidan) will give a slice of data and queries, and we'll schedule a follow-up SE deep-dive next week.
[07:10] Aidan Lee: Sounds good. One last question: we use internal SSO (SAML) - how long to set that up for Dedicated?
[07:17] Jordan Kim: Typically 1-2 business days for initial SSO integration with Dedicated; Private sometimes takes longer depending on network setup. We'll include a runbook in the security pack.
[07:28] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[07:31] Jordan Kim: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs.

End of transcript.
